# The Lattice
[italic]We did not build them. We have stopped asking who did.[/italic]
Six black pillars stand on six islands of deck around the spot where Caelestinus Central was later built. Nanotrasen's first survey found them already there. Their glyphs matched no alphabet. They drew no power anyone could measure. Nothing marked them: not drills, not cutters, not time. The survey logged them as relics of an earlier people and moved on.
When Kyphrus fell, the pillars woke.
Their glyphs lit. A violet field rose around each one. And the [textlink="Unmooring" link="WFLoreUnmooring"] stopped, exactly, at the edge of their reach, as though it had been told to.
Whoever raised them knew the star would fall. Whoever raised them built for it, and then left.
## What is known
- There are six. The charts call them [bold]Alpha[/bold], [bold]Beta[/bold], [bold]Gamma[/bold], [bold]Delta[/bold], [bold]Epsilon[/bold] and [bold]Zeta[/bold]. They stand on the corners of a hexagon nobody measured out, accurate to the centimetre. - Each wears different glyphs. Each sits inside a field that looks very like the one a Scion raises at the end of its song. Nobody likes that. - They are armed. Their guns are not ours. They answer whoever fires on them, and they do not miss. - The drones are theirs. Near a working anchor they mend it and guard it. Far from one, they forgot what they were for, and now they mend the only fault they can still find: us.
## What is not known
- What they are made of. Shards chipped from a pillar's base by a fallen ship became [color=#d070ff]exotic matter[/color]. The same matter is found in the rock past the anchors' reach. Nobody has asked the obvious question in writing. - How to make another. Smaller copies can be built from exotic matter. They hold a little. They are not the same. - What happens if they all go dark.
## From the record
[italic]Lattice survey team, voice log, Delta anchor. The team leader's name has been removed at the family's request.[/italic]
"The glyphs aren't decoration. They're moving. Slowly. Like a clock. Dev thinks they're counting."
"Counting what?"
"Down, he says. He won't say from what."
[italic]The survey team requested reassignment the following week. The request was granted. Delta's glyphs have been photographed every day since. They have not repeated.[/italic]
